```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```
```{r}
# A variable can contain multiple elements and this can be through the use of using vectors. Vectors are specified by using the function c().

my_first_vector <- c(1,5,9)
print(my_first_vector)

# Vectors can contain all types of variables but in the vector, they need to all be the same type of variable (eg can not use a numeric and logical variable in the same vector).

character_vec <- c("Hello","this","is","a","character","vector")
print(character_vec)

logical_vec <- c(TRUE,FALSE,TRUE)
print(logical_vec)

# Existing variables can be put into a vector by using the variable names

x <- 1
y <- 2
z <- 3

xyz_vector <- c(x,y,z)

cell_ID <- c(cell_ID_1,cell_ID_2)
treated <- c(treated_1,treated_2)
num_cells_before <- c(num_cells_before_1, num_cells_before_2)
num_cells_after <- c(num_cells_after_1, num_cells_after_2)

print(cell_ID)
print(treated)
print(num_cells_before)
print(num_cells_after)
```
```{r}
# The values in a vector can be accessed using an index which refers to the position of the value within the vector.

# Indices are indicated within square brackets [].

nice_food <- c("cheese", "chicken","potatoes")

print(nice_food[1])
print(nice_food[2])
print(nice_food[3])

all_my_pets <- c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")
new_animal <- all_my_pets[4]
print(new_animal)
```
```{r}
# A data frame is a table where each row is a single record and each column is a specific piece of information.

my_data_frame <- tibble( fruit = c("apple","pear","banana"),
                         length = c(22,30,55),
                         weight = c(150, 165,170)
                         )
print(my_data_frame)
```
```{r}
# Existing vectors can be put into data frame columns.

fruits <- c("apple", "pear", "banana")
lengths <- c(22, 30, 55)
weights <- c(150, 165, 170)

my_data_frame <- tibble(
  fruit = fruits,
  length = lengths,
  weight = weights
)


print(my_data_frame)
```
```{r}
# Use the function gt() instead of print() so that the formatting is nicer.

my_data_frame <- tibble(
  fruit = c("apple", "pear", "banana"),
  length = c(22, 30, 55),
  weight = c(150, 165, 170)
)

gt(my_data_frame)
```
```{r}
radiation_experiment <- tibble(
  cell_ID = cell_ID,
  treated = treated,
  num_cells_before = num_cells_before,
  num_cells_after = num_cells_after
)

gt(radiation_experiment)
```
```{r}
# A CSV file contains data that is in the form of a data frame.

# CSV files can be read in R by using the read_csv function and assigning this to a variable. The gt() function will then form the data frame.

weather <- read_csv("data/weather_data.csv")
gt(weather)
```
